name: SFLT-1 : PIGFRATIO FOR PRE-ECLAMPSIA PREDICTOR
interpretation:
NICE 2016 recommendation to diagnose suspected Pre-eclampsia

Note:
1. sFlt-1 : PLGF ratio is intended to be used with clinical judgment & other investigations to diagnose Pre-eclampsia in
suspected cases. It may be used for testing pregnant women from 20 weeks gestation up until the time of delivery.
2. The test is not recommended for conditions other than suspected Pre-eclampsia.
3.Severely elevated sFlt-1/PlGF ratios (>655 at <34+0 weeks; >201 at ≥34+0 weeks) have been associated closely
with the need for delivery within 48hrs and should prompt close surveillance

Comment
Pre-eclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and fetal/neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide. Clinical diagnosis and definition of PE is commonly based on the measurement of non-specific signs and symptoms, principally hypertension and proteinuria. They have very low predictive value for PE and its associated adverse outcomes. It has been reported that excessive placental production of soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase recptor-1 (sFlt-1), an antagonist of Vascular endothelial growth factor & Placental growth factor (PLGF) contributes to pathogenesis of PE. Increased serum levels of sFlt-1 and decreased levels of PLGF, thereby increased sFlt-1 : PLGF ratio can be detected in the second half of pregnancy in women diagnosed to have PE or other placenta related disorders (IUGR or still birth). The ratio may also be used to help predict Pre-eclampsia, Eclampsia and HELLP syndrome in the short term. Using sFlt-1 :PlGF ratio in addition to standard clinical assessment could result in a faster and more accurate diagnosis of Pre-eclampsia, and better risk assessment for adverse outcomes.

Usage

  • Women with established criteria associated with an increased risk of developing PE
  • Women who are identified to be at risk as a result of a Uterine artery Doppler examination
  • In a woman with PE already confirmed (high blood pressure & proteinuria) the sFlt-1 : PlGF ratio may be useful to determine the severity of the disorder.
